site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

run_plan.goal: Critique the UX of the Tessera docs system by validating the primary docs/tutorial flow, the reference navigation patterns, and recovery/variant states (version switcher, search, theme).
run_plan.summary: Start on index.html to validate global navigation, version switching, search entry, and theme toggle. Then traverse the primary adjacent docs pages (sql-select.html and reference.html) to verify the multi-column reference layout, left TOC behavior, and on-page outline. Finally, validate a representative set of function/operator detail pages (DATE_TRUNC, JSON_EXTRACT, REGEXP_MATCH, ROW_NUMBER, plus operators.html) including version history expansion and example navigation.
assumptions: All listed HTML files are reachable locally and contain consistent global header controls (version switcher, ⌘K search, theme toggle).
reference.html uses a three-column layout with an expandable/collapsible left navigation tree and an on-this-page outline in the right column.
Function pages share a common structure (signature, parameters, return value, examples, errors, version history) and include an 'Edit this page on GitHub' link.
Mobile layout may differ, so critical interactions from desktop should be repeated at least on index.html and one reference/detail page.
risk_hotspots: Global header controls: version switcher (ux-7 is a small select with missing/no label), ⌘K Search (ux-8 small tap target), theme toggle (ux-9 small tap target) — risk of hard-to-use/tap targets and accessibility issues.
Reference page navigation: left deep TOC expand/collapse and scrolling sync with center/right content (reference.html).
Canonical function page structure: DATE_TRUNC examples/results tables and 'Version history' collapsible panel (function-date-trunc.html).

Function parameter usability: parameters tables across function-* pages and any missing labels (prescan flags a missing_input_label on the version select element, but also warrants checking if any page has unlabelled inputs).
Cross-page anchor/outlines: right-side on-this-page outline behavior on reference.html and on function pages.

phases.title: Index: global navigation, versioning, search, and theme
phases.objective: Validate the primary entry experience and global controls from index.html, including variant selection and UI state changes.
key_checks: Use version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1) and confirm the page content updates to the selected release (or clearly indicates it does not).
Trigger ⌘K Search and verify it opens/closes correctly and returns relevant results/links within the local doc set.
Toggle dark/light theme via 🌓 and confirm syntax highlighting and contrast remain readable on code blocks.
Verify primary CTAs: 'Get started →' and 'View reference' navigate to the intended pages/sections without dead ends.
exit_criteria: Version switcher interaction is repeatable and results in either visible content/version callout changes or an explicit no-op explanation.
Search overlay/interaction opens, accepts input (if applicable), and navigates to at least one known target page (e.g., DATE_TRUNC, Operators, SELECT).
Theme toggle changes styling without breaking layout (code blocks remain readable).
Both CTAs navigate successfully to reference.html and/or the correct start section.

phases.title: Reference hub: 3-column navigation and browsing by category
phases.objective: Validate reference.html's navigation model (left TOC tree, center content, right outline) and ensure category browsing works as expected.
key_checks: Expand/collapse left TOC nodes (e.g., Functions → subgroups; Operators → categories) and confirm the active node highlights correctly.

Use popular links in the center section (e.g., DATE_TRUNC, REGEXP_MATCH, JSON_EXTRACT, ROW_NUMBER, Operators, Data types, SELECT statement) and confirm they load the corresponding function/operator/sql pages.
Verify right-side 'on-this-page' outline updates as the user scrolls or as content changes (if it is interactive).
Confirm version callout 'What’s new in v2.4' is visible and consistent with the current version selection from the header.
exit_criteria: Left TOC expand/collapse works without losing scroll position or causing broken states.
At least 3 center popular links successfully navigate to the expected detail pages among the target set.
Right-side outline is present and either updates with scroll or provides reliable anchor navigation.

phases.title: Tutorial/detail path: SELECT statement and core syntax flow
phases.objective: Validate sql-select.html as the main tutorial/reference bridge, including readability of clauses and example navigation.
key_checks: Verify clause order and explanations are readable; confirm there are no broken code blocks or missing sections (Syntax through Examples).
Test any in-page navigation (section jumps if present via outline anchors).
Check 'WITH' (CTE) section content for clarity and whether example code/results render correctly.
exit_criteria: All major sections listed in prescan headings are visible and accessible via scrolling/anchors.
Any available on-page navigation behaves consistently and does not misalign with content.

phases.title: Representative function pages: structure, examples, errors, version history
phases.objective: Deep-validate the shared function detail pattern using DATE_TRUNC as the canonical example and cross-check two other function types.
key_checks: For function-date-trunc.html: confirm signature and parameter table correctness; expand/collapse 'Version history'; validate 'Errors' content is clearly separated.
Verify examples (3 cases on DATE_TRUNC) show corresponding SQL and result tables and that tables are readable and not horizontally clipped.
Cross-check JSON_EXTRACT: ensure it communicates auto-parsing behavior and JSONPath usage clearly; confirm examples include extract/indexing cases.
Cross-check REGEXP_MATCH: confirm it clearly states RE2 syntax and truthiness behavior; ensure flags parameter description is readable.
Cross-check ROW_NUMBER: confirm it distinguishes ties (vs RANK) and that the signature shows required OVER clause parts.
Validate 'Edit this page on GitHub' link presence and that it is not misleading (even if external).
exit_criteria: DATE_TRUNC: version history collapsible works; errors section present; example result tables render cleanly.
Each other function page loads fully with signature/parameters/return value/examples visible and no layout breakage in result tables.

phases.title: Operators and data types: browse depth and table clarity
phases.objective: Validate two non-function reference pages for navigation and content density handling.
key_checks: operators.html: verify category sections (Arithmetic/Comparison/Logical/String/JSON/Array) and that operator precedence description is readable.
Confirm operator tables show example/result consistently and are not truncated on mobile widths.
data-types.html: validate presence of storage size/value ranges table and that numeric type aliases and defaults are readable.
Use left TOC interactions (if present) to jump between categories (from global navigation/within layout).
exit_criteria: Operator and data-type tables are readable with no major clipping and section headers are clearly distinguishable.
At least one intra-page browsing interaction works (e.g., scroll/outline/anchors) or category headings can be reliably found.

phases.title: Mobile viewport repeat: critical paths only
phases.objective: Repeat the most failure-prone interactions from desktop on mobile to validate tap targets and layout.
key_checks: index.html: verify tap targets for Tessera/Docs/Reference, version select, ⌘K Search, and 🌓 remain usable; ensure the header does not overlap content.
reference.html: verify left TOC (expand/collapse) remains accessible and does not obscure the center content.
function-date-trunc.html: verify version history collapsible and example tables are usable without horizontal scrolling issues.
exit_criteria: No critical controls become unusable (can open search, switch version, and toggle theme).
Reference navigation remains operable on mobile and detail sections remain readable.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages listed in prescan (9 total).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls per key page: version switcher, ⌘K search, theme toggle, reference left TOC expand/collapse, popular link navigation, and function version history collapsibles; additionally validate example result tables and error callouts.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile for index.html, reference.html, and function-date-trunc.html (header controls, TOC access, and collapsible/table rendering).

notes: Use the prescan evidence to avoid claiming tutorial-specific forms or dialogs (none detected). Focus on navigation, search, version/theme states, and content rendering (tables/code).
Given prescan layout warnings about small tap targets, prioritize mobile verification of header controls before deeper content critique.

observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.title: JSON_EXTRACT — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub JSON_EXTRACT Extract a value from a JSON document using a JSONPath expression. JSON_EXTRACT navigates a JSON document with JSONPath. The result is a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Signature JSON_EXTRACT(document JSON, path TEXT) → JSON Parameters Name Type Required Description document JSON required A JSON document. Strings will be auto-parsed if they contain valid JSON. path TEXT required A JSONPath expression beginning with $. Return value A JSON scalar or composite value. Use ::TEXT or ::INTEGER to cast to a SQL type. Examples 1. Extract a string field Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"user":{"name":"Ana","plan":"pro"}}'::JSON, '$.user.name'); Result json_extract "Ana" 2. Extract from JSON column in table Copy SELECT id, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type')::TEXT AS event_type, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.amount')::INTEGER AS amount FROM events WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type') = '"charge.succeeded"'; Result id event_type amount ev_8Hk2nF charge.succeeded 2500 ev_M5kQ2nF charge.succeeded 1899 3. Array indexing Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"items":[10,20,30]}'::JSON, '$.items[1]'); Result json_extract 20 Errors Common errors: invalid_path: malformed JSONPath expression. type_mismatch: attempting to cast a non-scalar JSON value to a primitive SQL type. Version history 3 entries ▼ v2.4JSONPath now supports filter expressions like $.items[?(@.price > 100)]. v2.2Improved index access performance for large arrays by ~3×. v1.5Added in v1.5. Related functions JSON_VALID JSON_AGG JSON_OBJECT JSON_ARRAY JSON_TYPE CAST ON THIS PAGE Signature Parameters Return value Examples Errors Version history Related © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. Some lookbehinds no longer supported. v1.5Added flags parameter. v1.0Added in initial release. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. Copy WITH ranked AS ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) AS rn FROM events ) SELECT user_id, type, created_at FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1; Result user_id type created_at u_001 login 2026-05-11 14:22:08 u_002 purchase 2026-05-11 12:45:01 3. ROW_NUMBER is the simplest of the ranking window functions. Unlike RANK, ties do not share a number. Signature ROW_NUMBER() OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] ORDER BY ...) → BIGINT Parameters Name Type Required Description OVER clause WINDOW required Defines the window. PARTITION BY is optional; ORDER BY is required. Return value BIGINT starting at 1 for each new partition. Examples 1. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. Top-N per partition A common pattern: find the latest event per user. observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

Keyboard/control usability was partially evidenced: the overlay shows the search input area with a placeholder, but no direct typing or result filtering was performed in this step.

Identified additional UX/accessibility signals from the overall page state: multiple controls (e.g., “Tessera”, “Docs”, “Reference”, “Tutorials”, “Download”, “GitHub”, “⌘ K Search”, and “🌓”) are flagged by the harness as small tap targets; also a “missing_input_label” warning appears for a head-area select (likely the version selector).

observation.title: JSON_EXTRACT — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 📝 Edit this page on GitHub JSON_EXTRACT Extract a value from a JSON document using a JSONPath expression. JSON_EXTRACT navigates a JSON document with JSONPath. The result is a JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null). Signature JSON_EXTRACT(document JSON, path TEXT) → JSON Parameters Name Type Required Description document JSON required A JSON document. Strings will be auto-parsed if they contain valid JSON. path TEXT required A JSONPath expression beginning with $. Return value A JSON scalar or composite value. Use ::TEXT or ::INTEGER to cast to a SQL type. Examples 1. Extract a string field Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"user":{"name":"Ana","plan":"pro"}}'::JSON, '$.user.name'); Result json_extract "Ana" 2. Extract from JSON column in table Copy SELECT id, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type')::TEXT AS event_type, JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.amount')::INTEGER AS amount FROM events WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(payload, '$.event.type') = '"charge.succeeded"'; Result id event_type amount ev_8Hk2nF charge.succeeded 2500 ev_M5kQ2nF charge.succeeded 1899 3. Array indexing Copy SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('{"items":[10,20,30]}'::JSON, '$.items[1]'); Result json_extract 20 Errors Common errors: invalid_path: malformed JSONPath expression. type_mismatch: attempting to cast a non-scalar JSON value to a primitive SQL type. Version history 3 entries ▼ v2.4JSONPath now supports filter expressions like $.items[?(@.price > 100)]. v2.2Improved index access performance for large arrays by ~3×. v1.5Added in v1.5. Related functions JSON_VALID JSON_AGG JSON_OBJECT JSON_ARRAY JSON_TYPE CAST © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
